definition_zh: 立志；渴望达到；谋求职位；向往
definition_en: to desire strongly to achieve something high or to become a certain kind of person
core_image: 一个孩子趴在窗台上，看远处塔楼的尖顶，一直看到脖子发酸
scene: 她十六岁那年看完一本关于深海的书，从此决定要做海洋生物学家。She aspired to study the deep sea years before any university had replied.
sceneCN: 这里 aspire 指「立志要达到某个高目标」（第 1 个义项：朝高处立志）；句意为在还没有任何大学回信之前，她早已立志研究深海。图中可辨识物件：远处的塔尖、被翻旧的深海书、窗台的手印、尚未拆封的回信。

pos.zh: 立志；渴望（与 to、after 搭配）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示行为的名词后缀构成，语义由「朝高处呼气」转为「志向」
由动词词干加表示人的后缀构成，语义由「渴望」转为「谋求者」
由现在分词转为形容词，语义由「正立志」转为「有志于进入某行的」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，语义由「志向」转为「带有志向色彩的、励志的」

senses.title: Aim at a distant goal
senses.definition: to set one's hopes on a goal that lies well beyond present reach
senses.definitionCN: 把希望放在一个远超出当下能力所及的目标上
senses.example: She aspired to study the deep sea long before any university had replied.
senses.exampleCN: 在还没有任何大学回信之前，她早已立志研究深海。
senses.why: the Latin verb means to breathe toward something, so aspiring is aiming one's whole breath at a far object.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此立志就是把整口气都朝一个远处的对象呼去。

senses.title: Seek a particular office
senses.definition: to try to obtain a post, title or place that others may also want
senses.definitionCN: 试图取得一个别人也想要的职位、头衔或位子
senses.example: Three deputies aspired to the vacant chair.
senses.exampleCN: 三位副手都想坐上那把空出的椅子。
senses.why: the Roman picture was a candidate walking around to court votes, and that political sense never left the word.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的图景是候选人四处奔走拉票，那层政治意味从未离开这个词。

senses.title: Want to become a certain person
senses.definition: to wish to turn oneself into a particular kind of person or worker
senses.definitionCN: 希望把自己变成某一类人或某一种从业者
senses.example: He aspired to be a country doctor rather than a famous surgeon.
senses.exampleCN: 他想做乡村医生，而不是名医。
senses.why: the aim is no longer a thing but an identity, and the same upward breath is directed at a self to be built.
senses.whyCN: 目标不再是一件东西，而是一种身份，同一口向上的气被呼向一个待建成的自己。

senses.title: Emulate a standard
senses.definition: to measure oneself against a model or a standard set by others
senses.definitionCN: 拿自己与别人立下的榜样或标准相比照
senses.example: Her early drawings aspired to the plainness of the old masters.
senses.exampleCN: 她早期的素描向往古代大师那种朴素。
senses.why: breathing toward a model is how skill is acquired: one imitates before one can invent.
senses.whyCN: 朝榜样呼气正是技艺获得的途径：先模仿，才谈得上创造。

senses.title: Hope for an ideal condition
senses.definition: to long for a better condition such as peace, fairness or quiet
senses.definitionCN: 渴望更好的处境，如和平、公平或安宁
senses.example: The whole valley aspired to nothing more than a quiet winter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个山谷向往的不过是一个安静的冬天。
senses.why: the object can be a condition rather than a possession, which is why the word suits public hopes.
senses.whyCN: 对象可以是一种处境而非一件所有物，因此这个词适合表达公共的希望。

senses.title: Rise physically
senses.definition: to rise or tower upward, said of buildings, smoke or terrain in older prose
senses.definitionCN: 向上升起或高耸，旧时用于建筑、烟或地形
senses.example: The spire aspired so high that the bells could be heard across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那尖顶高耸，钟声在河对岸都听得见。
senses.why: this is the plain physical sense of breathing upward, before the word was narrowed to desire.
senses.whyCN: 这是「向上呼气」最朴素的物理义，出现在词义收窄为「渴望」之前。

senses.title: Pronounce with a breath
senses.definition: to utter a consonant with a audible puff of breath, as in the p of pin
senses.definitionCN: 发音时带出一股听得见的气，如某些词里那个辅音之后的气
senses.example: In this dialect speakers aspire the t at the end of a word.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方言里，说话人会把词尾那个辅音发成送气音。
senses.why: phonetics kept the literal meaning, since the sound really is a breath pushed out.
senses.whyCN: 语音学保留了字面意思，因为那个音确实就是被推出来的一口气。

senses.title: Long for something intensely
senses.definition: to desire something intensely, often used with after in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想要某物，正式文字中后面常接一个介词
senses.example: The exiled poet aspired after one more sight of the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 流亡的诗人心心念念再看一眼那些山。
senses.why: when the object is out of reach, the verb carries pure longing rather than a plan.
senses.whyCN: 当对象无法到手，这个动词就带着纯粹的渴，而不是一份计划。

intro.en: Aspire comes from Latin aspirare 'to breathe upon, to blow toward', built on ad- 'to' and spirare 'to breathe'. The deeper origin of spirare is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁 aspirare「朝……呼气、向……吹」，由 ad-「向」与 spirare「呼吸」构成。spirare 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the tie proposed to a root for 'to blow' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「吹」的词根相联系，只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare gave aspirare 'to breathe upon', and metaphorically to favour someone or to strive toward something.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare 构成 aspirare「朝……呼气」，并比喻为「眷顾某人」或「向往某物」。

items.en: Roman writers used the verb for courting support, so the word entered English with a political edge before it meant plain longing.
items.cn: 罗马作家用这个动词表示争取支持，因此这个词带着政治色彩进入英语，早于它表示单纯渴望。

items.en: English took the verb in the fourteenth century, at first in the sense of rising or towering, then of hoping for high things.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收了这个动词，先表「升起、高耸」，再表「向往高处之物」。

items.en: Grammarians applied the same word to consonants pronounced with breath, which is the oldest physical layer kept in technical use.
items.cn: 语法学家把同一个词用于带气发音的辅音，这是最古老的物理层在技术用语中的保存。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of spirare and the dating of the hopeful sense): no citation fixes when rising became longing, and any Indo-European form offered for spirare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（spirare 的更深来源与希望义的确切年代）：没有书证能定住「升起」何时变成「渴望」；凡为 spirare 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates words built on the same breathing verb; group two separates verbs of wanting by how reachable the object is.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「呼吸」动词的词；第二组按对象的可达程度区分表示「想要」的动词。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus spirare: to breathe a feeling into someone, hence to fill them with enthusiasm.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「入」加 spirare 构成：把某种感受吹进别人心里，因而指激发热情。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out' plus spirare: to breathe out one's last breath, hence to come to an end.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「出」加 spirare 构成：呼出最后一口气，因而指终了、到期。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus spirare: to breathe as one, hence to plot together in secret.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 spirare 构成：同呼一口气，因而指暗中合谋。

entries.definition: Per- 'through' plus spirare: to breathe through the skin, that is, to sweat.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per-「穿过」加 spirare 构成：透过皮肤呼气，也就是出汗。

entries.definition: From Latin asper 'rough': harshness of surface or manner, with no connection to breathing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 asper「粗糙」：表面或态度的粗硬，与呼吸无关。

entries.definition: To want something with a real chance in view; it can be modest, while aspiring is always aimed high.
entries.definitionCN: 在还看得见机会的情况下想要某事；可以很小，而立志总是朝高处。

entries.definition: To want something, often without any plan to get it; it carries no effort.
entries.definitionCN: 想要某物，往往没有任何获取的计划；不含努力。

entries.definition: To feel a deep and often painful desire; the feeling outweighs the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 怀着深沉而常带痛的渴望；感受压过了目标。

entries.definition: To try actively to find or obtain something; it names the activity rather than the ambition.
entries.definitionCN: 积极地设法找到或取得；指活动，而不是抱负。

entries.definition: To struggle hard toward something; it stresses the exertion, while aspire stresses the height of the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 奋力朝某处挣扎；强调使力，而 aspire 强调目标的高度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare 'breathe': to breathe toward something far away.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare「呼吸」：朝远处某物呼出一口气。

normal.en: The family runs aspire, aspiration, aspirant, aspiring, aspirational.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖动词、名词、谋求者、现在分词形容词与励志形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the objects: aspire to a post, aspire to become, aspire after honour.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出对象：谋求职位、渴望成为、渴求荣誉。

normal.en: The political origin survives in aspirant, the person who wants the seat.
normal.cn: 政治来源仍活在「谋求者」这个名词里，指那个想要位子的人。

normal.en: Phonetics keeps the oldest sense: an aspirated consonant is a sound carrying a puff of breath.
normal.cn: 语音学保留了最古老的意思：送气辅音就是带出一口气的音。

abstract.en: Picture a child on a sill looking at a spire until the neck aches.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子趴在窗台上望着塔尖，直到脖子发酸。

abstract.en: Picture a kite pulling at the string before the wind has lifted it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只风筝在风还没把它托起时就已经把线拉紧。

abstract.en: Picture a seed leaning toward a light it cannot yet reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子朝它还够不到的光倾斜。

examples.en: Many young engineers aspire to work on the rover team.
examples.cn: 许多年轻工程师立志进入火星车团队。

examples.en: He aspired to the mayor's office for twelve years.
examples.cn: 他谋求市长之位谋了十二年。

examples.en: The village aspired after clean water more than after roads.
examples.cn: 村民对干净用水的渴求胜过对道路的渴求。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a 斯派尔」——一口气朝远处送去 → 立志、渴望

root: 拉丁 aspirare「朝……呼气」= ad-（向）+ spirare（呼吸）；spirare 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one breath: it is aimed at a goal, at an office, at an identity, at a model, at a condition, at the sky itself, at a consonant, and finally at something simply out of reach.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一口气展开：这口气被呼向一个目标、一个职位、一种身份、一个榜样、一种处境、天空本身、一个辅音，最后呼向一件单纯够不到的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watcher at a window breathing toward a distant spire.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗前的观望者朝远处塔尖呼出一口气。

branches.en: THE AIM AND THE CONDITION: a distant goal and a wished-for state are the same upward breath.
branches.cn: 目标与处境：远处的目标与所盼的处境，是同一口向上的气。

branches.en: THE CONTESTED SEAT: others want it too, and the political origin shows.
branches.cn: 被争的位子：别人也想要，政治来源在此显现。

branches.en: A SELF TO BUILD: a person and a model are both aims one grows toward.
branches.cn: 待建的自己：人与榜样都是会长过去的靶子。

branches.en: THE LITERAL RISE: stone and smoke go up before desire is meant.
branches.cn: 字面的升起：在「渴望」之前，石头与烟先往上升。

branches.en: BREATH WITHOUT AN OBJECT: a consonant's puff, and longing that has given up on arrival.
branches.cn: 没有对象的气：辅音的那一口气，以及不再指望抵达的渴望。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb with a prepositional prefix, and both parts still build English words, so it reads clearly by morphemes.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个带介词前缀的拉丁动词，两部分仍在构成英语词，因此可以按语素清楚读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare gives spirit, inspire, expire, respire and conspire; ad- 'to' appears in adapt, adhere and admire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare 衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、respire 与 conspire；ad-「向」见于 adapt、adhere 与 admire。

items.example: The prefix gives the breath a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给这口气一个方向。

items.example: The root is the breathing itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是呼吸本身。

items.example: The wind breathed upon the cliff.

items.structure: aspirare passing into French and English
items.example: She aspired to the research post.
items.exampleCN: 她立志争取这个研究职位。

items.example: An aspiring novelist worked the night shift.
items.exampleCN: 一位有志写小说的人上夜班。
四名谋求者进入候选名单。

items.example: His aspiration was to teach in the hills.
items.exampleCN: 他的志向是在山里教书。

items.example: The brochure was aspirational, not literal.
items.exampleCN: 这本宣传册是在引发向往，而非写实。

items.example: Children aspirate the first consonant too strongly.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们把第一个辅音送气送得太重。

items.example: The valley inspired the whole score.
items.exampleCN: 这条山谷激发了整部乐曲。
